subject: Cutover phases, QPS calibration & egress wiring for NimbusAI private GPU fleet
messages:
From: NimbusAI Ops <ops@nimbusai.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeColab DC Ops <dcops@edgecolab.net>
Date: 2026-05-07T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Private fleet requirements: baseline QPS + cutover windows

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for running the private deployment workshop last week. Per our call, I'm sending the baseline performance targets and our preferred cutover timing so your team can propose a sizing + phase plan. Key points: 

- Steady-state target: 80 inference QPS (1 request = average 450 tokens) with 95th percentile latency target <= 350ms.
- Peak windows: 3x baseline for 20 minute bursts, expected 2x baseline for scheduled report jobs (daily).
- Model family: customer will run a 70B-family open model (quantized FP16/INT8 variants) with KV cache enabled.
- Network: crossconnect to our on-prem colo via a 10Gb redundant link, prefer egress headroom of 4 Gbps to start.
- Cutover target week: 2026-06-14 to 2026-06-18 with a two-phase canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%).

Attached: nimbus-qps-profile.csv (sample traffic histogram). We'd like a short runbook for the cutover that lists acceptance criteria (latency, error rate, throughput) and rollback criteria. Also confirm estimated GPU count and a proposed warmup schedule.

Can you confirm who from Redwood will drive the test windows with our DC ops?

Thanks,
--

Hi all —

Sizing notes (conservative / optimized):

Assumptions common to both: avg request 450 tokens, model ~70B quantized; steady-state 80 QPS => ~36k tokens/sec inbound user work. We assume 65% KV cache hit for customer traffic after warmup. Batching effective size target 16-24 on GPUs. Network serialization overhead ~8%.

1) Conservative (safety-first)
- GPU type: A800 equivalent (48GB).
- GPUs: 12 (3 shards of 4 GPUs) with headroom for 1.5x sustained load.
- Estimated sustained tokens/sec per GPU: 3.5k (after batching & cache) => cluster ~42k tokens/sec capacity.
- Expected p95: 280-360ms depending on batch alignment; recommend admission control to prevent queueing beyond 120ms.
- Network egress: reserve 5 Gbps to allow spikes + model payload overhead.

2) Optimized (cost-aware)
- GPU type: A800 / H100 mix if available for peak lanes.
- GPUs: 9 (3 shards of 3 GPUs) tuned with aggressive batching and pre-warmed KV cache.
- Estimated sustained tokens/sec per GPU: 4.5k => cluster ~40.5k tokens/sec; relies on 75% cache hit-rate.
- p95: ~250-320ms in controlled conditions.
- Network egress: 4 Gbps baseline with burst allowance to 6 Gbps for 2 minute windows.

Operational recommendations:
- Warmup plan: 6-hour progressive prefill for KV cache then 30-minute smoke with synthetic traffic at 30% of peak before canary.
- Canary gating metrics: p95 latency, 5xx rate <= 0.2%, CPU/GPU utilization thresholds, and error-per-minute. Move 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 30-60 minute observation windows.
- Autoscale: prefer scheduled burst lanes + admission control rather than autoscale on immediate QPS to avoid oscillation.
- Warm pool: keep a 1-GPU hot spare per shard for fast absorption during spikes.

I'll attach a quick calc sheet (not attached here) but estimates map to the csv you provided. Happy to adjust numbers once we validate KV cache hit expectations with Nimbus.

-karthik

Team —

Draft cutover phases and acceptance/rollback criteria below. I'll convert into a runbook doc (redwood-cutover-runbook-v1.md) and share a link.

Phase 0 — Dress rehearsal (2026-06-12)
- Mirror traffic for 1 hour at 1.2x baseline. Acceptance: p95 < 380ms, 5xx < 0.5%.
- Network test: saturate crossconnect for 2 minutes to validate egress policing and LACP failover.

Phase 1 — Canary 5% (2026-06-14)
- Synthetic warmup + 30-minute observation. Gate: p95 delta < +15% vs baseline, error-rate <= 0.2% absolute.

Phase 2 — Canary 25%
- 60-minute observation. Gate: CPU/GPU steady state < 80% sustained, no progressive increase in queue depth.

Phase 3 — Progressive ramp to 100%
- Move 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% in 2-hour windows. If any gate fails -> rollback to previous percentage and open incident.

Rollback criteria (immediate):
- p95 > 450ms for 3 consecutive intervals OR 5xx spike > 1% sustained for 10 minutes.
- Network packet loss > 0.5% or link flaps detected on crossconnect.

On-call & responsibilities:
- Redwood infra on-call: Karthik (lead) / Mina (backup) — runbook execution and scaling actions.
- Redwood ops: Jonas — cutover coordinator and acceptance arbiter.
- Nimbus/DC: Priya / EdgeColab primary contact — network-level failovers and crossconnect config.

Next steps: Karthik to share the final GPU count once you decide conservative vs optimized. Grace & I will produce the runbook and the canary traffic generator script. Priya/EdgeColab to confirm dress rehearsal time slot.

Jonas Weber
